comments.note: EXCELLENT: Pattern consistency across all 5 entity types. The same multi-value pattern is applied uniformly (Ships/Modules use builderFactionIDs, Shields/Engines/Weapons use makerRaces), making the codebase highly maintainable and predictable.

EXCELLENT: Backward compatibility implementation handles 3 scenarios flawlessly: (1) new array format, (2) old string format with space-separated values, (3) old key containing array from intermediate rebuild. This is sophisticated defensive programming.

EXCELLENT: API preservation strategy prevents breaking changes. Original single-value methods (getBuilderFactionID, getMakerRace) return first element, while new multi-value methods (getBuilderFactionIDs, getMakerRaces) provide array access. This is textbook backward-compatible API evolution.

MINOR SUGGESTION: ShipsExtractor.php line 270 logs 'WARNING' for ships with no builder faction, but since it's handled gracefully with a default, consider changing to 'INFO' or 'NOTICE' for consistency with the actual severity level.

MINOR SUGGESTION: Magic string 'unknown' is used as fallback in ShieldDef, EngineDef, and WeaponDef (3 locations). Consider adding KnownFactions::FACTION_UNKNOWN constant for centralized management in a future refactoring.

MINOR SUGGESTION: New methods lack detailed PHPDoc comments explaining WHY multi-faction support is needed (game data contains compound entries like 'argon teladi'). Adding this context would help future maintainers understand the business requirement.

MINOR SUGGESTION: Test coverage could be enhanced with explicit test case for empty string handling in fromArray(). The code handles this correctly (defaults to generic/unknown) but explicit test would document the behavior.

GOLD NUGGET: The multi-value faction/race pattern is now established and could be abstracted into a trait or base class method if more entities need similar support in future. Recommend documenting this as a reusable architectural pattern in project manifest (tech-stack.md) for future reference. This pattern successfully handles: (1) array storage, (2) backward-compatible single-value API, (3) new multi-value API, (4) hasMultiple() predicate, (5) space-separated parsing, (6) format migration in fromArray(), (7) array_intersect filtering in Finders.

SECURITY ANALYSIS PASSED: No SQL injection risk (no database), no XSS risk (server-side library), no user input handling vulnerabilities, explode on space is safe (controlled data from XML files), array operations are safe and properly typed. Code follows secure coding practices.

PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS PASSED: Array operations (intersect, explode, filter) are efficient for expected dataset sizes. No N+1 issues. Lazy loading of FactionDefs appropriate. No premature optimization. ShipDefs::getFactions() could cache results but given collection size (~256 ships) this is unnecessary optimization.

ARCHITECTURE COMPLIANCE VERIFIED: Follows x4-core Collection-Item pattern, Extraction-Builder pattern, consistent with existing codebase conventions. No technical debt introduced. Future-proof design supports more than 2 factions without code changes. Maintains x4-core manifest constraints (sync file I/O, no databases, strict types).
